newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds enjoy mixed fortunes, eyes on ECOFIN.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds enjoy mixed fortunes, eyes on ECOFIN.

text.p: Irish government bonds enjoyed mixed fortunes in thin late trade on Thursday as the market focused its attention on this weekend's informal meeting of European Union finance ministers in Dublin, dealers said.
Ministers from the 15-nation bloc are to meet to discuss Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

"Irish bonds are not greatly changed from Wednesday's close. On balance, we are slightly lower against both UK gilts and German bunds," one dealer said. "At this point, we are awaiting news from this weekend's ECOFIN meeting in Dublin."
The meeting, which takes place on Saturday, will focus on the relationship between those countries joining a single currency and those who remain outside and the legal framework for the euro.
In the afternoon ministers will discuss the so-called stability pact to ensure fiscal discipline after the changeover to the single currency.

By 1505 GMT, the 8.00 percent bond due 2000 had eased seven pence from Wednesday's close at 104.62 to yield 6.55 percent while the 8.00 percent bond due 2006 had risen five pence from the close at 105.15 to yield 7.12 percent.
Dealers said a close eye is also being kept on the U.S. ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on September 24 amid talk of a possible rise in U.S. rates.
